families.note: BORN NOT FOR SALE 2026-08-24. This is not a feed and there is no collector behind it. It is one dated reading of 46 CFR part 541, the US rule that says what a container demurrage or detention bill must carry. The whole of what we hold is printed on the family page for free: 20 required items, 3 items we counted as required and withdrew, and 4 thirty-day clocks, each beside the regulation's own words. SAMPLE STATUS IS unknown ON PURPOSE, NOT BY OVERSIGHT: the estate's sample block ends every not-for-sale sample with 'these rows are a slice of the file, and the file goes back further than these rows do'. That sentence would be false in both halves here, so no sample file is written and the page says in its own words why the pill is right. Every number on the page is read at build time out of revenue-2026/projects/free_time/rules/us-container-billing.json, and 26 quoted phrases are checked word-for-word against the saved regulation text at revenue-2026/research/sources/title46-part541-2026-08-01.txt on every build -- one mismatch refuses the build. THERE IS NO UPLOAD SERVICE and the page promises none. CORRECTION 2026-08-24: sample status moved from unknown to on-page. Unknown said we could not answer; the answer is settled and permanent. There is no file behind this page, so there is no sample and there never will be one. The new value is checked at scripts/check_site.py -- which demands this page carry the sentence 'the whole of what we hold is printed on this page', read out of the builder's own constant rather than retyped -- and drawn on the directory card by scripts/build_hub.py. Changing this field alone changes nothing a reader sees: the card is generated, so the hub has to be rebuilt in the same change or the directory keeps saying the sample is not ready yet. CORRECTION 2026-08-25, APPENDED not edited: the sentence above about the page saying "why the pill is right" described a page that no longer exists, and while it stood the page said "Sample not ready" twice -- counted off the built bytes -- under a directory card that said "All of it, free". Moving this field to on-page on 2026-08-24 moved the card and could never move the page, because the eyebrow was drawn from the module's own ready flag and not from here. scripts/render_family.py now reads this field and prints the same words the card does, from one constant both import. The page's honest-box paragraph no longer quotes the eyebrow at all. One consequence taken on purpose and not by surprise: with the phrase gone, scripts/pipeline.py scores this family's sample gate pass instead of fail, on 27 named rows counted off the page itself. That reading is the true one and it was checked before the words were changed.

families.name: Grid peak calls, sealed the day before and scored the day after
families.buyer: Factories and data centres whose grid bill is set by their load during a few peak hours
families.who: Factories and data centres whose grid bill is set by their load during a few peak hours.
families.note: BORN NOT FOR SALE 2026-08-25 (dated from the newest rows in the recorder's own store, not from this machine's clock, which reads two different days depending which setting is asked). WHAT THE LANE DOES: a factory or data centre's grid bill for a whole year is largely set by how much it was pulling during a handful of hours -- the hours when the whole grid was at its busiest. Once a day, for the day after, the recorder reads the grid operator's own published forecast and writes down one of two things: cut your load, or ordinary day. That is a call. It is sealed with a fingerprint at the moment it is made, before anyone knows how the day went, and it is scored afterwards against the operator's own record of what actually happened -- wrong calls included, one row per call. NOTHING HAS EVER BEEN SOLD HERE and there is no price on the page. The lane's own spec describes a possible paid product later (the calls themselves, ahead of the day) but that is a separate decision that has not been made, and the recorder's own can_we_sell() answers no and names the reasons. The page is the free scoreboard, and it is free forever: the whole record is on it. NO SAMPLE FILE, ON PURPOSE, AND sample_status IS 'fail' RATHER THAN 'on-page' FOR A REASON. There is no file behind this page to slice, so there is nothing to sample and the pill saying 'sample not ready' is correct. It is NOT 'on-page' either: on-page means the whole of what we hold is printed on the page, and that is false here -- the page prints every call, but the recorded grid load behind the threshold rule (hundreds of days of it) is counted on the page, not printed on it. Calling it on-page would be a sentence a stranger could check and find untrue. THERE IS NO UPLOAD SERVICE, no form, no account and no self-serve anything -- this estate's platform is not ours to add one to. The only way in is an email thread with a person, which is what the contact block on the page says. NO NUMBER, DATE, PRICE, GROUP, CADENCE OR BUYER IS TYPED INTO THE PAGE. scripts/slice_peak_call.py reads group, cadence, buyer and price out of this row with no fallback, and reads every call, date, hour, megawatt figure, fingerprint and count out of revenue-2026/var/peak_call.db read-only at build time. It recomputes every call's fingerprint with the recorder's own function on every build and refuses to write the page if one no longer matches, because the only claim this record makes is that it was not edited after the fact. It also reads the addresses the recorder fetches out of the recorder's own code and refuses to build unless each one carries a permission note whose verdict is 'allowed' -- a grid operator that refuses to be read is never named here as a source of anything. THE ZEROS ARE THE CONTENT, NOT A GAP. At 2026-08-25 no call had been scored yet and no call had told anyone to cut, and the page says both in words rather than printing an empty counter. The recorder's own written bar refuses a hit rate under 5 warnings, and refuses to call the record sellable under 60 scored calls, 5 warnings and 90 days of public record -- all three written down on 2026-08-24 while the answer to all three was still no. The page carries that bar and no percentage. cadence_long is NOT stored in this row on purpose: the module recounts it off the sealed calls at build time, so the page cannot go stale even if this row does. STILL TO WIRE, FOR WHOEVER MERGES THIS: there is no peak-call entry in scripts/family_status.py. That is harmless while this row lives in a fragment, because scripts/build_site.py reads catalog.json only and this family never reaches dist/. The day this row is merged into catalog.json it stops being harmless: the built page will carry no read-date stamp and scripts/check_built.py will mark it as a page with no read date. The store is at an absolute path, which _store_path() already supports. CORRECTION 2026-08-25, appended not edited: this row was written as sample_status "fail" and that was the wrong word. "fail" means a sample file exists and is wrong; there is no sample file here and there is never going to be one, because the record on the page IS the product. The page said both "sample not ready" and "all of it is on the page" in the same paragraph, which are the two halves of a contradiction — a stranger reads "sample not ready" as a file that is coming, and no file is coming. Status moved to "on-page", the same word free-time and verified-record carry, and the page now says the sentence the honesty gate demands instead of quoting a pill it cannot see. Nothing about the price changed: it was not for sale before this correction and it is not for sale after it.

families.name: A checked record of what a person says about their own work
families.buyer: Expert witnesses and fractional executives who want their own claims checked against the places those claims are written down
families.cadence_long: One dated reading of five sentences of federal law, re-checked word for word against the saved copies on every build
families.short: What we may say about a person
families.who: Expert witnesses and fractional executives who want their own claims checked, and anybody wondering what we would ever publish about them.
families.note: BORN NOT FOR SALE 2026-08-24. Verified Record is an OPT-IN listing. A person asks to have the things they say about their own work checked against the places those things are written down, each claim is read twice by two methods that never see each other's answer, and a claim only appears as checked when both readings find it. NOBODY IS LISTED WHO DID NOT ASK. There is no state anywhere in the lane meaning a person's claim is false: the only three words are verified, not checked and withdrawn, and the shared scan engine/scoreboard/verdicts.assert_no_false_state is run on this lane and on the shared package at build time to prove no fourth one was ever added. NOTHING HAS BEEN SOLD, no price is printed anywhere on the page, and the catalog price stays 'Not for sale yet' until that changes. Intake is an EMAIL THREAD with a person: there is no form on the page and no service to send a file to, because a web service that takes files is platform code this lane may not write and reading them by hand is operator labour it may not create. SAMPLE STATUS IS on-page AND IT IS ENFORCED, NOT ASSERTED: the lane's store at revenue-2026/var/verified_record_data.db holds no people, no claims and no listings, so there is no file to sample, and what the page prints is the whole rulebook. scripts/slice_verified_record.py reads that store read-only on every build and REFUSES TO BUILD if a row appears in any of its tables, because the sentence 'the whole of what we hold is printed on this page' stops being true the moment somebody is listed. Every rule sentence on the page is the lane's own words, pulled out of its code at build time rather than retyped, and the five sentences of 15 U.S.C. 1681a and 1681e are re-checked word for word against the saved copies in revenue-2026/research/sources on every build -- one mismatch refuses the build. The wording guard that would stop a page passing judgement on a person is run in BOTH directions on every build: a judging line built out of the guard's own first banned phrase must be refused, and a plain 'we could not confirm' line must clear. Removal is unconditional and immediate and the page says so in the code's own words; the money is recorded as owed back in the same call, and paying it out is an operator action because nothing in this build moves money outward.
